utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mrs. Rajic, this man with his hands in his pockets who started to speak, who is that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKA RAJIC
utterances.text: That's my husband Zvonko Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The one in the middle?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKA RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And the lady behind him, is that you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKA RAJIC
utterances.text: Probably, I was blond then. Yes, it's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it's you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: INTERPRETER: "We have one fact, the conflict from Gornji Vakuf spread all over the weight of these territories, in middle Bosnia, the municipality of Travnik. We are the HVO from Busovaca and this conflict spread to all these territories of middle Bosnia, municipality of Travnik. We are the HVO from Busovaca, and this territory belonged to the municipality of Zenica, this border. At the moment, according to some negotiations from Geneva, the municipality of Travnik goes up to the River Bosna. Probably they found out that the border was the River Bosna itself and they reinforced the entrance to Lasva, and they are saying that this is the municipality of Zenica, and that it will stay that way. As I have said before, we Croats will agree with every map that will be decided on at the highest level. That will come from Geneva. Whether it be the municipality of Zenica or Travnik, we will agree with it. We can't change any map or border that they make. We want peace and we will wait as people wait for the game to be over, the football match to be over, so that we know the game is over and the final results. That is what we're waiting for."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, I think we can stop there for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mrs. Rajic, your husband used sports terms, he was waiting for the match to be over, but we see that he did not live to see the end of it. Can you explain something to the Court for another ten minutes, and we can continue tomorrow. You said that Serif Patkovic had killed your husband and you said that he had killed all the people in a sadistic manner, he would talk to you in a friendly manner, eat and drink and then go out and kill the people. Did I show you yesterday the Slobodna Bosna paper, this week's edition?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKA RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And who did you see in the papers?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKA RAJIC
utterances.text: Serif Patkovic himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I should like the following text to be handed out. And yesterday, thanks to the Registry, we succeeded in translating portions of the text, and I would now like to ask the usher to hand the text around, and a copy for the transcript and for the interpreters. This will be Defence Exhibit, would you assign it a number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video is D438, and the transcripts are 438A. This document which has been given to us is D439.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document, you made a signal to me to tell me that it was not you on the tape, it was some, another lady, a neighbour. Madam, would you take the, look at the page that you have before you. May we place Patkovic's photograph on the ELMO, please, so that everybody can see? Mrs. Rajic, is the man who killed your husband and all the others in Lasva on this picture?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKA RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the man, that's Patkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You recognise him?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKA RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: He is a Colonel in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Have you ever heard that he was punished for his crimes?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKA RAJIC
utterances.text: No, no, unfortunately never.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm going to read some of the parts that have been translated. The paper is the Slobodan Bosna of the 7th of November, 1998, where Colonel Patkovic, Serif, has given an interview. May we have it on the ELMO, please? "Colonel Serif Patkovic, 30-year-old former commander of the controversial 7th Muslim Brigade, he was awarded the Golden Lilly, who in 1994, to Hadji Izetbegovic, handed a decree as being the honorary commander, is today one of the 1.000 wartime invalids, has for the first time, after a long silence, decided to reveal to our editor in detail the background to key war developments, particularly the unsuccessful attempts to lift the blockade of Sarajevo." After this headline in paragraph 3, it states, "The 7th Muslim Brigade was established towards the end of 1992 by Halil Brzina, Mahmut effendi Karalic and effendis Adilovic and Celikovic from Travnik and Kakanj." I am going to read the introduction to the text. "The former commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, under whose command the brigade was awarded the titles of glorious and gallant, Colonel Serif Patkovic has kept his silence for years, already. He says that he is reassembling the mosaic of the war, which passed like a film. The battle cry, Tek-bir Allah-u-ekber, with which the members of this brigade paraded through Zenica, went into battle against the Bosnian crags, began and ended their troop reviews, was synonymous with the 7th Muslim Brigade. It was said that this battle cry froze the blood in the enemy's veins, that before engaging in battle the troops said their own dzenazas, prayer for the dead, that they were sad if they survived because Allah had not wanted them. Such and similar mythical stories were told as an integral part of the way things are interpreted here." And on the next page we have a picture with the title Colonel Serif Patkovic, Mahmut ef. Karalic, Alija Izetbegovic, and Sakib Mahmuljin. So this is the inscription underneath the photograph of the people. That is the caption.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And Mr. President, I think this is a good time to break for today, until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'm sure that viewing these pictures was extremely painful for the witness, as it was everybody here. I suggest we stop now and remind you that tomorrow morning the Trial Chamber, with a different panel of judges and other work, will be involved in another case, and so, we will resume tomorrow at 2.30. Mrs. Rajic, try to rest and we will resume tomorrow at 2.00, 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 5.30 to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 18th day of November, 1998 at 2.30 p.m.
